products.product_name: Thermally Processed Concentrated Vegetable Juice Pulp/ Puree
products.conditional_article: Processed tomato concentrates and tomato puree or paste

named_ctr_articles.basis: listed finished processed tomato concentrate; source ppm
listed finished processed tomato concentrate; source ppm

named_ctr_articles.article: Tomato puree, paste, powder, and cocktails
named_ctr_articles.basis: ON DRIED TOMATO SOLIDS BASIS, NOT AS-SOLD WET PRODUCT

products.legal_definition: FSSR §2.3.13/§2.3.17 permits fruit or vegetable concentrated puree. A specific finished TOMATO puree/paste must additionally be identifiable under §2.3.14. Industrial preservative, container form, doubled soluble-solids concentration and permitted additions require lot-specific review; the general category is not automatically tomato.
required_positive_evidence: Production lot botanical identity proves ONLY ripe tomatoes, not general vegetable blend; §2.3.14 finished tomato puree/paste identity independently established
Finished soluble-solids assay proves >=9% tomato puree or >=25% tomato paste plus §2.3.13/§2.3.17 doubled solids where applicable
Lab result/report calculates Copper 100 mg/kg ON DRIED TOMATO SOLIDS BASIS, not mg/kg as-sold; establish tomato dry-solids correction
Lead 1.5 mg/kg and Tin 250 mg/kg named processed tomato concentrate articles require actual finished concentration and sample basis
Verify permitted preservatives/thermal treatment, pack fill, operative amendments, contamination panel and lot test; no automatic PASS
negative_controls: Mixed vegetable puree and carrot/beetroot/ginger pastes are not named tomato puree or paste
Food category FSSR §2.3.13/16/17 cannot automatically be replaced by §2.3.14
Industrial use with preservatives is not blanket evidence that actual finished article is tomato concentrate
Copper on dried tomato solids is not mg/kg as-sold wet product
Lead and Tin on processed tomato concentrate cannot be assigned to nonconcentrated §2.3.16
A first named source does not establish a complete contaminant panel or an actual lot PASS

products.conditional_article: Tomato puree (copper-only initial route, not assumed processed concentrate)

named_ctr_articles.article: Tomato puree, paste, powder, and cocktails
named_ctr_articles.basis: ON DRIED TOMATO SOLIDS BASIS, NOT AS-SOLD WET PRODUCT

products.legal_definition: FSSR §2.3.16 permits industrial-preserved fruit/vegetable puree without defining a processed tomato concentrate. The copper article is qualified only if the actual finished product independently meets §2.3.14 Tomato Puree criteria; Pb/Tin processed tomato concentrate articles are NOT promoted for this un-concentrated category.
required_positive_evidence: Confirm §2.3.16 actual finished tomato puree rather than blended vegetable puree and legally match §2.3.14 tomato puree finished form
Verify tomato source, mechanical processing, any preservatives (Appendix A), pack and whether puree reaches >=9% total soluble solids
Copper 100 mg/kg is ON DRIED TOMATO SOLIDS BASIS, requiring analytical conversion; not as-sold wet-product concentration
Do not apply Lead 1.5 / Tin 250 processed tomato concentrates automatically: §2.3.16 does not require concentration
Verify further metal and contaminant articles, current amendments and actual lot lab results, without whole-product PASS
negative_controls: Mixed vegetable puree and carrot/beetroot/ginger pastes are not named tomato puree or paste
Food category FSSR §2.3.13/16/17 cannot automatically be replaced by §2.3.14
Industrial use with preservatives is not blanket evidence that actual finished article is tomato concentrate
Copper on dried tomato solids is not mg/kg as-sold wet product
Lead and Tin on processed tomato concentrate cannot be assigned to nonconcentrated §2.3.16
A first named source does not establish a complete contaminant panel or an actual lot PASS

products.conditional_article: Food product containing any of the above mentioned food articles
products.legal_definition: FSSR 2.11.5 states Pan Masala MAY contain betelnut; betelnut is NOT mandatory. Aflatoxin composite-product source operates only if actual finished Pan Masala contains a qualifying source commodity and falls within that named article.

named_ctr_articles.article: Food product containing any of the above mentioned food articles (including arecanut or betelnut)
named_ctr_articles.basis: qualifying actual arecanut/betelnut containing finished food; not unconditional Pan Masala

named_ctr_articles.article: Food product containing any of the above mentioned food articles (including arecanut or betelnut)
named_ctr_articles.basis: qualifying actual arecanut/betelnut containing finished food; not unconditional Pan Masala

required_positive_evidence: Actual finished Pan Masala formulation and bill of materials establish arecanut/betelnut as an ingredient; 'may contain' does not mean must contain
Supplier declarations and botanical identity tie betelnut to CTR 'Arecanut or Betelnut' article
Apply named composite-food aflatoxin total and B1 only after confirming scope and full finished matrix; separately assess other ingredient-specific constraints
Confirm operative CTR/FSSR amendments and legal testing/sample basis in the finished product
Actual production lot results and other mycotoxins/metals/pesticides prior to any complete compliance conclusion
negative_controls: Pan Masala without arecanut/betelnut cannot claim this route by its product name alone
Arecanut ingredient-only Total Aflatoxins 15 µg/kg is not the named finished composite-food 20 µg/kg
Arecanut ingredient-only B1 10 µg/kg is distinct from the composite article even where numbers coincide
FSSR total ash <=8% (dry basis) and acid-insoluble ash <=0.5% (dry basis) are not mycotoxin tests
No substitution of spices, coconut or sweeteners to invent a betelnut-based finished product
No automatic contaminant or laboratory PASS
